source_evidence: for investment advisory accounts with lower balances, small monthly fees like these can add up to a large percentage of the amount invested
answer: A robo-adviser may charge a subscription-based fee: a set recurring payment, often monthly, for the advisory services described in your agreement. Because this fee does not necessarily shrink when your account balance is small, it can take up a sizable share of your money. For example, the source explains that a $3 monthly fee on a $500 account would total $36 per year—more than 7% of the account’s value. Read the fee and service terms in the advisory agreement so you understand what you will pay and receive.
